record_type_quote: In this study, we repeated the analyses conducted by Vas and colleagues using the Dog ARS [ 14 ], addressing similar research questions and employing a similar design on new samples to examine evidence of the reliability and validity of the rating scale and to identify possible limitations.

targets.authors: Vas J., Topál J., Péch A., Miklósi A.
targets.title: Measuring attention deficit and activity in dogs: A new application and validation of a human ADHD questionnaire.
targets.evidence_quote: Of note, in examining the factor structure and external validity of the C Dog ARS we simultaneously aimed to determine the extent to which relevant findings obtained earlier [ 14 ] are replicable.
targets.outcome_quote: Our findings on external validity, specifically, age-related decrease in owner-rated inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, effect of training experience, and sex on these factors, complement earlier research. Vas and colleagues found associations between the inattention scale and age and training status, but no associations between hyperactivity/impulsivity and these variables.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm factor structure but explicitly distinguish original null hyperactivity/impulsivity associations from current associations with age/training; item means also differ. Confirmation of main findings/factor structure does not cover these tested contrasts. Lit et al. is an earlier replication discussed for context, not the designated retest.

reasoning: New dog samples explicitly re-test Vas et al. factor structure and external validity findings. Measure diagnostic limitations are extensions, not a verdict rendering the replication invalid.
